notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Declan Carlile has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 69:27 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 44:25 together.
Ville Koivunen is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve (hip surgery) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nico Myatovic has taken his spot beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.
Tyson Hinds has not dressed for the last 4 games. Pavel Mintyukov has taken his spot beside Tristan Luneau.
Laurent Brossoit was added to the roster on Nov 3.

ANA.head: The Ducks have a lot going for them
ANA.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Anaheim will be without Terry, Pittsburgh is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Koivunen. On top of that, Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Penguins can make it interesting if they get good looks.

PIT.head: The Penguins face a real test
PIT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Even though Anaheim will be without Terry, Pittsburgh is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Koivunen. On top of that, Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Penguins’ best way through is getting good looks.

story.head: The Ducks are rolling
paras: The Ducks have won four straight, and the Penguins (6-9-2) beat Los Angeles 5-2 last night. Going in, the Pens are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Ducks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 16th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.412) says: their chances are worth about .548, mostly because they’re 3-6 in one-goal games. The Ducks’ record (.559) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.485), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest) and get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st). The Ducks, by contrast, hound the puck on the forecheck (4th). The Penguins also rarely throw hits (lowest), so the Ducks hit a lot, but them mostly don’t. The Ducks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th), so the Penguins could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them. Anaheim has scored 3.76 goals a game, the fourth most in the league, and allowed 3.76, the third most.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 14 A / 17 P in 17 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 17 GP) has a team-high seven goals. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Cutter Gauthier (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 16 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-5-1 / .876 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh. Ville Husso (2-3-0 / .869 SV% in 4 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but is expected to start.

items.text: The Penguins have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk, Elmer Söderblom and Bryan Rust for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.

The Ducks are newly without A.J. Greer, and have been without Troy Terry and Tyson Hinds for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Penguins are missing more right now.
Cutter Gauthier has twelve goals on chances worth about 6.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Jackson LaCombe has a point in nine straight games.
